chunks: And Allah made His covenant and pledge a security, which He spread among His servants through His mercy, and a sanctuary in which they find rest in His protection, seeking the benefit of His asylum,
Therefore, there should be no deceit, cunning, or duplicity in it.
Do not enter into an agreement that allows for various interpretations, and do not rely on the ambiguity of words after the conclusion and confirmation (of the agreement).
Let not the hardship of a matter in which Allah's covenant has bound you, lead you to seek its annihilation without justification,
For indeed, your patience upon the hardship of a matter, hoping for its relief and the excellence of its outcome, is better than a treachery whose consequence you fear,
And that you are called upon by Allah for it, in which you cannot face your worldly life nor your hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on breaking a covenant due to hardship?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) grounds the political covenant in divine mercy, establishing it as a sacred trust ('dhimmah') that requires absolute integrity without the use of legalistic loopholes or deceptive interpretations. He warns against dissolving this bond due to temporary hardship, asserting that patient fidelity yields greater spiritual reward than the fear of divine retribution for treachery. This instruction reflects the Shia emphasis on 'amanah' (trustworthiness) as a core attribute of just governance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Allāh made His agreement and pledged the sign of security which He has spread over His creatures through His mercy and an asylum in which they stay in His protection and seek the benefit of nearness to Him.
Therefore, there should be no deceit, cunning or duplicity in it.
Do not enter into an agreement which may admit of different interpretations and do not change the interpretation of vague words after the conclusion and confirmation (of the agreement).
If an agreement of Allāh involves you in hardship do not seek its repudiation without justification,
because the bearing of hardships through which you expect relief and a handsome result is better than a violation whose consequence you fear,
and that you fear that you will be called upon by Allāh to account for it and you will not be able to seek forgiveness for it in this world or the next.
